claim: For every finite simple complete multipartite graph \(G=K_{n_1,\ldots,n_r}\) with \(r\ge 2\) and all \(n_i\ge 1\), the majority C-chromatic number satisfies \(\overline{\chi}_{\geqslant}(G)\le 2\), with equality exactly when every part size \(n_i\) is even. When equality holds, every majority C-coloring with two colors splits every part exactly in half between the two colors. Consequently the number of labeled optimal two-colorings is \(\prod_{i=1}^r \binom{n_i}{n_i/2}\), and the number up to interchanging the two color names is half of this product.
integrity: The universal proof is analytic. Exhaustive finite enumeration through order 8 is used only as an independent stress test of the statement and counting formula.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns finite simple complete multipartite graphs with at least two nonempty parts and the one-half open-neighborhood threshold. It does not treat non-complete multipartite graphs or other thresholds. The literature comparison cannot exclude an unindexed older equivalent under different terminology.
title: Majority C-colorings of complete multipartite graphs
